p.em: For a first cohort of champions, or a leadership walkthrough. Show, don't tell.

tr.td: Why we are here. The footer's sentence and the sign-in page's sentence. Nothing here is a side door.
Discover. Available to you; the chips; open one card; request one thing and watch it appear in the workspace.
A listing. The permission table, row by row. Ask the room what W1 means before saying it. Show the sign-off card.
The assistant. Ask a real question. Point at a claim and its chip. Answer the feedback question. Show a stopped answer if you can.
The brief. Start one live. Fill section 1, then open the composer in section 3 and drag two tools in; watch the ceiling, the road and the estimate change. Stop before filing.
Sign-offs and onboarding. The queue's counts; the four attestations; the six stages. Say who in the room is an owner and who could sign for AI security.
The guide. Open it as a leader, then as a builder. Run the tour. Ask it the leader's first question.
Close. Each person names one problem their team feels this month. The brief is due before the next meeting.

ac:rich-text-body.p: What to leave people with: the hub shows only what your role opens; an assistant reads and cites; an agent reads, and writes only when a named person says yes; a component is on the shelf only when two named people signed it; and the guide will walk you through any of it.
